text: Design a whole concrete frame in 3D, and see every step.
Meet Zeta Model Space, for NSCP 2015 and ACI 318.

beats.text: Start on Geometry. Type the bays, and the storey heights.
Regenerate, and the whole frame is built: beams, columns, slabs and footings.
Drag to orbit the model, from any side.
On Loading, scroll down to the earthquake section.
C a and C v come from the soil profile and the seismic zone.
R is the system factor, eight point five for a special moment frame. I is the importance factor.
Every ticked direction becomes its own load case.
Method B takes the period from the modal analysis, capped by the code.
Accidental torsion shifts each storey force by five percent of the plan.
Tick orthogonal effects, so every case also carries thirty percent of the other direction.
And the vertical component is folded into the combinations.
Generate. Sixteen earthquake cases, with the storey forces listed level by level.
Then wind. Set the basic wind speed, from the N S C P map.
Pick the exposure: suburban, open, or coastal.
Generate the wind cases, with the base shear in each direction.
On Analysis, choose how the frame is modelled.
Cracked sections reduce the stiffness of the concrete, as A C I requires.
Shear deformation adds Timoshenko shear flexibility.
P Delta adds the second order effect of gravity on the swayed frame.
A rigid diaphragm makes each floor move as one plate.
Now analyse the frame in 3D.
Every member: axial force, shears, torsion and moments, for every combination.
The support reactions, with a statics check. The applied loads and the reactions balance.
And the displacement of every node.
On Display, colour the members by stress.
Run the modal analysis.
Each mode, with its period, frequency, and mass participation.
Click 3 D, and watch the first mode move.
Pushover pushes the frame sideways, until it forms a mechanism.
Push in X, with an inverted triangle load.
The capacity curve plots base shear against roof displacement. Straight while elastic, it bends as plastic hinges form.
Every hinge is listed, in the order it forms.
Now design.
Design structure checks every member, against every combination.
Sixteen columns fail, and each one shows its ratio.
Click optimise. Sizes and bars are re-chosen, and the frame is analysed again.
Every member passes.
Open any row for its worked solution.
The bar layout, with the section drawn.
The capacity, by strain compatibility, step by step.
The biaxial check, with the clause cited.
And the bar selection, against the code limits.
Back on Display, turn the contour off,
hide the loads,
and show the reinforcement cages.
Pick which cages to see. Here: beams, columns and footings.
Every bar, exactly where it goes.
The plans are drawn for you.
Open a sheet,
and step through the set: framing plans, elevations, column and footing details.
Click P D F, and choose what goes in the report.
The design status,
the traceability, from load to bar,
worked solutions for every member,
and the drawings.
The appendix adds the modal,
and pushover results, because they were run.
Bind it as one P D F,
and generate. Five hundred and eighty-one pages, every check shown.
And Exchange sends the model to E tabs and STAAD, and every table to Excel.
